source.title: Hidden Breakthroughs in Language Model Training
source.authors: Sara Kangaslahti; Elan Rosenfeld; Naomi Saphra

page_placements.theme: Measurement and aggregation change apparent emergence

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites grokking as an example of a training breakthrough, but its experiments do not measure the grokking behavior or mechanisms named by any claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper measures directional and per-example loss breakthroughs, not training-versus-test accuracy, formation or removal of a grokking circuit, or a delayed generalization jump. Its results on these related training-dynamics measures are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The paper cites grokking (Power et al., Nanda et al.) only as background examples of breakthroughs. Its experiments measure directional and per-token loss breakthroughs with POLCA on 3-digit addition and Wikipedia language modeling. It reports no train-versus-test accuracy gap, no delayed generalization jump, no generalizing or memorizing circuit, and no weight-decay, dataset-size or optimizer manipulation. None of V1 to V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors also argue the results support the view that high-dimensional learning involves a series of breakthroughs at various scales.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes POLCA, a directional loss-decomposition and clustering method; it does not reproduce the original grokking method.
record.method_sensitivity: The fraction of detected hidden-breakthrough clusters varies with trajectory measure and basis choice; the random orthonormal basis yields 0.031, versus 0.304 for the random shuffled Hessian basis and 0.355 for POLCA.

fits_no_version.finding: On 3-digit addition, POLCA clusters reach carry homogeneity of 0.973, versus 0.514 for exact loss. Of POLCA clusters, 0.355 have breakthroughs after the exact-loss plateau at step 1000, versus 0.0 for exact loss. Results depend on trajectory measure and basis (random orthonormal basis: 0.031).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Directional loss decomposition reveals skill-specific breakthroughs (e.g. carrying) hidden in smooth aggregate loss curves.

fits_no_version.finding: In a 40M-parameter Wikipedia LM, POLCA projected-loss clusters show sudden changes tied to syntactic constructions while their exact-loss curves stay smooth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Language-model training contains many hidden, direction-specific breakthroughs obscured by the aggregate loss.

record.problems: The experiments use small models, and the arithmetic hidden-breakthrough results depend on the chosen trajectory measure and basis. No results test the listed grokking claims.
record.rows_left_out: The arithmetic carry-homogeneity result (POLCA value 0.973) and additional cluster-quality metrics in Appendix G, Table 8 are not listed as separate rows because they concern skill-cluster purity rather than the hidden-breakthrough measure. Other individual English clusters in Appendix K are also omitted; the paper provides illustrative examples rather than a separate aggregate result for each.

untested.parts: All of V1: no train/test accuracy trajectories, no delay, no dependence on training-set size.
All of V2: no generalizing or memorizing circuit, and no progress measure tested against a grokking jump.
All of V3: no grokking delay on non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
All of V4: a small 40M-parameter Wikipedia LM is trained, but delayed generalization is not measured.
All of V5: weight decay is fixed at 0.1, with no critical dataset size and no ungrokking.
All of V6: no comparison of algorithms across runs.
All of V7: no optimizer or floating-point controls.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is not an original source, but it cites both originals, and the 'phase transitions are everywhere' quote links it to Nanda et al. thematically only. The arithmetic task is 3-digit addition trained for one epoch with AdamW, which is not a grokking setup. The rows are method-comparison values and should not carry partial or absent states for any version.

versions.untested_parts: No training/test accuracy trajectories, overfitting, or dependence of delay on training-set size are measured.
The paper does not identify a generalizing circuit or memorizing components, or test whether a continuous measure anticipates a grokking jump.
No grokking-like delays on non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale/weight-norm interventions are tested.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is studied.
No efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking result is tested.
The study does not compare algorithms learned across runs.
No optimizer-instability or floating-point artifact challenge is tested.

relation.reason: Grokking appears as background motivation for studying breakthroughs; the experiments neither test nor use grokking itself.

tranche.reason: POLCA experiments measure directional loss changes and skill-cluster recovery, not delayed generalization or another defined grokking version.

source_check.notes: All eight rows are method comparisons or ablations, not evidence for a grokking version. The baseline wording denotes the plateau threshold, not a numerical comparator; the cited carry homogeneities are maxima over eligible clusters.
